text:
jamie_infra: Heads up — canary edge pool in us-west-2 started rejecting CUDA 12 images after the nightly container rebuild. Scheduler marks GPU nodes NotReady and pods CrashLoopBackOff. Seen on 3 distinct hosts so far. Anyone seeing the same?

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary-rollout-redwood-runtime: 6/6 pods failed -> rollback recommended :warning:

sara_sre: Logs? paste a failing pod's kubelet/dmesg if you have it.

jamie_infra: Paste from one host dmesg/kern.log: 
```
[  123.456789] nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol nvidia_register
[  123.456790] nvidia_uvm: Unknown symbol in module
[  123.456800] modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.15.0-1023-aws
```

mina_runtime: @jamie_infra this smells like kernel/driver ABI mismatch. We rebuilt the runtime images with GCC13 toolchain (to fix a build warning) last night — those images include libs compiled against newer kernel headers. Host drivers are older (525 series).

raul_ml: Also seeing NCCL init failures in job logs: "ncclCommInitRank failed: uninitialized or incompatible ABI" — likely same root cause. Jobs retried and consumed extra GPU-hours.

ops_lead: Immediate action: pause further canary rebuilds, rollback canary to previous image. jamie, can you do a rollback and cordon the 3 impacted nodes?

jamie_infra: Rolling back now: 
```
kubectl -n infra set image deploy/redwood-runtime redwood-runtime=ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:2026-03-14
kubectl rollout status deploy/redwood-runtime -n infra
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-45-17.us-west-2
```
Pods came back up on the old image. Nodes are still NotReady until we clear the module mismatch.

mina_runtime: Long term: we need a preflight matrix in CI that verifies container libnvidia vs host nvidia-smi driver. Quick check command to run in pods/nodes: 
```
# on node
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
# in container
ldd /usr/local/lib/libnvidia-ml.so | grep nvidia
```
If versions differ by major, fail the build.

raul_ml: Cost impact— I tracked affected jobs: ~25 GPU-hours wasted on retries in the last 6 hrs across training and infra tests. That hits team budgets. Can we billback or label these as infra incidents for chargeback?

ops_lead: We'll mark as incident and post cost report. But operationally we should consider two mitigations: 
- Pin builder GCC/toolkit version to match host-compatible ABI, OR
- Add a lightweight compatibility step that runs DKMS-style module build on node boot (or ship kernel headers in image) — but that adds node boot time.

sara_sre: Also need better rollout strategy: current canary is 10% of capacity and spread across AZs. For kernel/driver mismatches that won't help. Propose a kernel-driver matrix smoke test as part of node health check and failover policy to move GPUs to backup region if repeated failures.

jamie_infra: Filing infra ticket with logs, node IDs, and failing pod names. Planning a small patch: revert GCC13 switch in the runtime builder for now and add the driver-version preflight.

deploy-bot: [incident created] INFRA-3782: cuda12-runtime-rebuild-compat-fallout by jamie_infra

mina_runtime: I'll open a PR for the preflight check and link to INFRA-3782. Pinging @sara_sre for SRE test cases.

ops_lead: Good. For immediate safety: squash remaining canaries, cordon any nodes with mismatched modules, and schedule reboots after we deploy a compat image. Also allocate 5 spare GPUs in us-west-2 for high-priority jobs while we triage.

sara_sre: Noted. I'll adjust autoscaler policy to avoid draining capacity below critical thresholds while we fix. :thumbsup:

jamie_infra: Thanks. Will follow up with a runbook and timeline in INFRA-3782.

mina_runtime: small note — if we go the DKMS route, we should measure node boot 95th latency. That could affect scaling and cost.

raul_ml: OK — please also flag any training jobs that need rerun so data teams can reschedule.

ops_lead: Closing thread for now, keep updates in INFRA-3782. :white_check_mark:
